title: Stop tool hopping.
summary:
How to start with AI as a beginner: pick one tool and use it every day for a month.
Stop tool hopping. Pick ONE tool (Claude or ChatGPT, I don't mind which), list the tasks you hate doing and hand the repeatable ones to AI, then give it context: talk to it like a colleague and show it examples of what you want. Do that for a month and AI gets a lot easier than you thought.

guide: This is a one-month routine for getting comfortable with AI: you need one account with ChatGPT or Claude, and a list of tasks you dislike.
1. Pick one assistant, either ChatGPT (OpenAI) or Claude (Anthropic), and use only that one for the next 30 days.
1. Open it at least once a day, even for something small, so using it becomes a habit.
1. Write a list of the tasks you hate doing, such as replying to similar emails, summarising notes or tidying spreadsheets.
1. Mark the ones that repeat, and hand those to the assistant first.
1. Give it context before each task: say who you are, what the task is for and who will read the result, as you would brief a colleague.
1. Paste in one or two examples of what a good result looks like, so it can match the style and format.
1. When a prompt works, save it in a note (Notion or any notes app) so you can reuse it next time.
1. After a month, look back at your list and see which tasks now take you far less time.
Watch out: trying a new AI tool every week resets what you have learned, so stay with one tool until the month is over.

```
You are my AI onboarding coach. I am a beginner and I want to use one AI tool every day for 30 days. My tool is <ChatGPT or Claude>. My job or situation is <your role>. The tasks I dislike doing are <list 3 to 5 tasks>.
Please do the following:
1. Work out which of my tasks repeat and are best handed to AI first, and rank them.
2. For the top three, write a starter prompt template I can reuse. Each template must set the context (who I am, what the task is for, who reads the result), leave a place for me to paste one or two examples of what I want, and state the format of the answer.
3. Give me a simple 30-day plan with one small task per day, building from easy to harder.
4. Tell me how to keep a list of prompts that worked.
Constraints: plain English, British spelling, no jargon, and do not suggest I add other AI tools. Return the ranked task list, the three templates with <placeholders> I can fill in, and the 30-day plan as a table.
```
